text:
sara: FYI customer 123 is seeing AccessDenied when the ingest service tries to decrypt the envelope after assume-role. CloudTrail shows KMS denied for the assumed role. Any quick ideas?

alex: do we have the session policy that the STS assume-role returned? AccessDenied is usually either key policy denying the principal or the session policy strips kms:Decrypt.

ben: also worth checking grants. If they rely on a CreateGrant flow and the caller didn't surface the GrantToken, decrypt can fail, especially around key rotation.

kms-bot: CloudTrail event -> kms:Decrypt denied. Caller: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/ingest-role/session ; Key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222222:key/abcd-ef01 ; Error: AccessDeniedException

sara: session policy we apply is intentionally tight — only allows GenerateDataKey and Encrypt. We assumed Decrypt would be done by a separate decryptor service, but the pipeline decrypts in-process. Session policy snippet: ```{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Encrypt"],"Resource":"*"}
  ]
}```

alex: that explains it — for envelope decryption you need kms:Decrypt. Two pragmatic paths: 1) widen the session policy to include kms:Decrypt for the role, or 2) create a KMS grant for the assumed role and ensure the caller passes back the GrantToken when calling Decrypt. Grants can avoid changing session policies but need CreateGrant permissions on the key policy.

ben: note about grants + rotation: if the service created a grant and the CMK was rotated or rekeyed by the rotator, grants may become stale; also some SDKs need the GrantToken returned immediately and attached to the Decrypt call. If Decrypt is called without the GrantToken, KMS will not honor the grant until it has fully propagated.

sara: we don't want to relax session policies without sign-off. Quick question: will adding a key policy statement that allows arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/ingest-role kms:Decrypt be safe? Or do we need to reference the assumed-role ARN?

alex: key policy should reference the role principal (the role ARN), not the assumed-role STS ARN. Example: "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/ingest-role"}. If using conditions that match the session, you can also match "aws:PrincipalArn" in a condition to be explicit.

ben: sample create-grant command that worked for us in a similar case: ```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/redwood-data-key --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/ingest-role --operations Decrypt --retiring-principal arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/kms-rotator
``` Remember to return the GrantToken to the caller. Without returning the token, immediate Decrypt calls may still fail.

sara: ok trying grant approach as a fast rollback-free fix. I'll create the grant and wire the rotator to return the GrantToken to the pipeline call that performs Decrypt. If that works we'll follow up with a ticket to either update the session policy or adjust the key policy doc.

oncall: :thumbsup: ping me if escalates.

(some minutes later)

sara: update: created grant + surfaced token from rotator; ingest pipeline decrypt now succeeds. Root cause: session policy didn't permit kms:Decrypt. Grant was acceptable interim fix. We'll open a follow-up to update the pipeline docs and the CMK key policy to document allowed principals and grant usage.

alex: thanks for the quick triage. Also add note about encryption context — if caller sets EncryptionContext on GenerateDataKey, Decrypt must supply the same context or KMS will deny. That bit often trips cross-service calls.

sara: good call — we saw encryptionContext in the logs earlier. Will add to the ticket.

ben: adding ticket: SEC-4821 to track policy + docs + rotator behavior for grant tokens.

sara: closing this thread, will update once SEC-4821 is implemented.
